what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat serious fungal infections throughout your body. It works by killing or stopping the growth of harmful fungi. Your doctor may prescribe it if you have a weakened immune system, if other antifungal medicines have not worked, or if you cannot tolerate other treatments. It is given in a hospital or clinic setting through an IV (intravenous) line.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a healthcare professional through a vein (IV infusion) in a hospital or clinic. You will not give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion usually takes about 2 hours, though your doctor may adjust the timing based on how well you tolerate it. Do not try to speed up or slow down the infusion on your own. Tell your nurse right away if you feel pain, burning, or swelling at the IV site.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your kidneys are working. The typical dose ranges from 3 to 6 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once a day. Your healthcare team will adjust your dose if needed. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by healthcare professionals in a clinic or hospital, missed doses are managed by your medical team. If you miss a scheduled infusion appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to double up on doses. Staying on schedule is very important to treat your infection properly.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home as it is prepared and given by healthcare professionals. The pharmacy or hospital stores the unmixed medicine in a refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Once the medicine is mixed and ready for infusion, it should be used within 6 hours if kept at room temperature, or within 24 hours if refrigerated. The mixed medicine must never be frozen.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, including vitamins and supplements, because many drugs can interact with this medicine. Avoid taking other medicines that can harm your kidneys, such as certain antibiotics (like gentamicin) or blood pressure medicines, without your doctor's approval. Do not use any new over-the-counter medicines or supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Avoid activities that could increase your risk of infection, such as being around people who are sick.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: sudden chest pain or tightness, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, rapid or irregular heartbeat, severe chills or shaking during or after your infusion, high fever, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, muscle cramps or weakness, decreased urination or dark-colored urine, unusual bruising or bleeding, severe nausea or vomiting, or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash or hives. Also call your doctor if you notice any new symptoms or if your infection does not seem to be getting better.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working against the fungal infection right away, but you may not feel better immediately. It often takes several days to weeks before you notice improvement in your symptoms. Your doctor will do regular blood tests and check-ups to monitor how well the medicine is working and to watch for side effects. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment even if you start to feel better.
special_populations: Kidney problems: This medicine can affect your kidneys. Your doctor will monitor your kidney function with regular blood tests and may adjust your dose if needed. Drink plenty of fluids unless your doctor tells you not to. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as this may affect how your body handles the medicine. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially kidney problems. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: This medicine can be used in children, including babies, and the dose will be carefully calculated based on the child's weight. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine should only be used during pregnancy if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor before breastfeeding.
